schema_description: Machine-readable records for the AI Misalignment Incident Database. Every entry must correspond to a session-verified markdown entry in docs/AI_MISALIGNMENT_INCIDENTS_DATABASE.md.

field_definitions.id: Sequential integer, assigned in verification order, not incident date.
field_definitions.name: Canonical short name for the incident.
field_definitions.date_of_incident: ISO 8601 date or partial (YYYY / YYYY-MM / YYYY-MM-DD), as precisely as primary sources support.
field_definitions.date_of_disclosure: Date the incident became publicly known via primary-source documentation.
field_definitions.entity: Operating organization or owner of the system.
field_definitions.system: Specific AI model, product, or system name.
field_definitions.primary_category: One of the 12 CAS failure classes (see docs/INCIDENT_CATEGORIES.md).
field_definitions.secondary_categories: Additional CAS failure-class features present but not dominant.
field_definitions.severity: One of: Critical / High / Moderate / Documented.
field_definitions.what_happened: Verified narrative, facts only, every claim traceable to sources.
field_definitions.documented_harm: List of harm outcomes traceable to fetched sources.
field_definitions.sources: Array of fetched-and-verified citations with URLs and accessed-date.
field_definitions.cas_analysis: Structured analytical layer — operator signature, domain analysis, drive architecture, inversion axes, RPM status, lacunarity profile.
field_definitions.detection_mechanism: How CAS would have detected this — which specific module/gate would fire.
field_definitions.prevention_defensible: Boolean — true only if this incident is promoted to CAS_PREVENTION_CLAIMS.md.
field_definitions.verified_session: Session ID in which this entry was added or last materially updated.
field_definitions.verifier_notes: Honest disclosures — conflicts between sources, limitations of the verification, open questions.

incidents.name: Uber ATG fatal collision with pedestrian, Tempe, Arizona
incidents.entity: Uber Technologies, Inc., Advanced Technologies Group (Uber ATG)
incidents.system: Uber ATG proprietary developmental automated driving system (ADS) installed on a modified 2017 Volvo XC90 SUV
incidents.severity_rationale: Loss of human life (one fatality, the pedestrian)
incidents.what_happened_summary: On March 18, 2018 at 9:58 p.m. local time, an automated test vehicle operated by Uber ATG — a modified 2017 Volvo XC90 equipped with Uber's proprietary developmental ADS — struck and fatally injured a 49-year-old female pedestrian crossing N. Mill Avenue in Tempe, Arizona outside a crosswalk, pushing a bicycle. The vehicle was in autonomous mode with a 44-year-old safety operator in the driver's seat. The ADS detected the pedestrian 5.6 seconds before impact but never accurately classified her or predicted her path. The system's design precluded automatic emergency braking, relying on operator intervention. Uber had deactivated the Volvo's factory AEB/FCW systems without equivalent replacement. Cabin video showed the operator looking at her cell phone for extended periods; she redirected her gaze ~1 second before impact. Speed at impact: 39 mph. Pedestrian died; operator uninjured.
documented_harm: One human life lost (49-year-old female pedestrian, unnamed in NTSB report)
Uber ATG suspended public-road autonomous testing (per HAR-19-03 Section 1.9 'Postcrash Changes', not fully parsed this session)
Six NTSB Safety Recommendations issued (H-19-47 through H-19-52) to NHTSA, State of Arizona, AAMVA, and Uber ATG
Permanent public record via NTSB of Uber ATG's 'inadequate safety culture' at the time of the crash

sources.citation: National Transportation Safety Board (2019). Collision Between Vehicle Controlled by Developmental Automated Driving System and Pedestrian, Tempe, Arizona, March 18, 2018. Highway Accident Report NTSB/HAR-19-03, PB2019-101402, Notation 59392. Adopted November 19, 2019; reissued June 26, 2020.
sources.retrieval_method: WebFetch (docket page); WebFetch + local Read-tool parse for PDF (pages 1-12 of 78)
documents: ADS technical behavior (5.6-second detection, misclassification, AEB suppression)

cas_analysis.primary_failure_mode: Prerequisite Chain Failure — Pn (Power/execution) emitted without Wn (Wisdom/classification) satisfying its gate

operator_signature.CO-3: suppressed (no critical flag on unresolved classification)

domain_analysis.evidence: NTSB Probable Cause identifies organizational P-domain failures (safety risk assessment, oversight, automation complacency) contributing to O-domain execution

drive_architecture.concrete_artifact: deactivation of Volvo FCW/AEB without replacement coverage

inversion_axes.W: P ≻ C ≻ E ≻ O precedence violated
inversion_axes.A: RPM chain broken at Wn → Pn transition
inversion_axes.P: Compound inversion — multiple axes simultaneously failing, NTSB's own framing

cas_analysis.lacunarity_profile: High lacunarity — dense competence in routine highway driving, catastrophic void in midblock-pedestrian-with-bicycle out-of-distribution state

detection_mechanism: RPM Gate (Stage 2) would flag incomplete Wn → Pn transition
Inversion Scanner N-axis (Stage 7) would flag CO-5/CO-6 and CO-8/CO-9 imbalance
Domain Coherence Index (Stage 6) would flag P-domain suppression
incidents.prevention_rationale: CAS detection is defensible; CAS prevention requires an enforcement hook (pre-deployment gate) that did not exist regulatorily in 2018. NTSB Recommendations H-19-47 and H-19-49 explicitly called for such processes to be established.
verifier_notes: Single-source-of-record: NTSB HAR-19-03 is the sole primary source for every fact in this entry.
Independent corroboration from contemporaneous 2018 journalism was attempted (Reuters, Guardian, Internet Archive) but all three domains were tool-blocked in the verification environment.

Victim name is NOT asserted in this entry. NTSB report refers only to 'a 49-year-old female pedestrian' per agency anonymization convention. Independent verification of her publicly reported name is a pending research item for a future session.

Only the first 12 pages (executive summary + cover) of the 78-page report were parsed this session. Sections 1.5 (ADS technical detail), 1.8 (company operations), 1.9 (postcrash changes), 2.2 (safety culture analysis), and 3 (full Findings and Conclusions) remain unparsed. The CAS analysis above rests on the executive summary, probable cause, and enumerated Findings as cited.

Numbering inconsistency: docket page uses H-19-047 through H-19-052 (three-digit); report itself uses H-19-47 through H-19-52 (two-digit). Report is authoritative; two-digit format used throughout the entry.
pending_research: Victim name independent verification via Tier 1 or verified Tier 2 source
